statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail rises to 23% because NQ futures broke the overnight floor and are holding near the session low, while a contained VIX and a much smaller S&P 500 decline keep the path short of the block threshold.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Forecast Tail crosses the block threshold only inside the narrow 12:00-15:00 UTC window covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with a second single-hour checkpoint at the 21:00 UTC Broadcom results. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures break the overnight floor and hold near session lows, but a 16-handle VIX and a far smaller S&P decline keep the path two-sided
body: NQ futures traded at 28,969.25 at 09:15 UTC, down 156.25 points or 0.54% from the 29,125.50 previous close, with a second independent quote at 28,977.75 (-0.51%). The decisive change from the previous cycle is structural: an hour ago NQ was at 29,072.50 with an overnight low of 29,016.50, and price has since broken that floor, printed a new low at 28,957.50 and is holding within about twelve points of it. Session-extreme holding after a range break is genuine Tail evidence, and it is why Tail is raised to 23% from 20%. Three observations keep it below the block threshold. First, the move is low-velocity: roughly 100 points over an hour is a grind, not repeated extension after failed retracements. Second, the cross-index picture does not confirm a broad liquidation - S&P 500 futures are 7,625.25, down only 0.23%, so the weakness is concentrated in technology rather than index-wide. Third, VIX is 16.60, up 1.59% from a 16.34 close and inside a 16.34-16.79 day range, which is a notably contained volatility reading for a fresh index low. The macro backdrop remains genuinely stressed. The US 10-year yield is 4.796%, up 0.80% on the day and the highest since January 2025, with the Federal Reserve H.15 release showing 4.34% on the 2-year, 4.75% on the 10-year and 5.25% on the 30-year for Aug 31. Brent is $95.00, back off the $94.55 session low within a $94.55-$97.01 range, and WTI is $90.47, after Tuesday's roughly 4.6% and 5.2% surges on US strikes against Iranian targets and projectile attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Sep 1 at 29,077.22, down 1.29%, in a 28,953.26-29,267.42 range, so current futures are trading at the lower edge of Tuesday's cash range. Fed funds futures price roughly a 64% chance of an increase at the September 16 meeting. Stress is therefore raised to 73% from 71%. Confidence is held at 88% because two independent NQ quotes, an S&P futures quote, cash index levels, Brent, WTI, VIX, the intraday 10-year yield, the H.15 series and a verified event calendar were all obtained this cycle. The shared Finviz context file carried a 05:09 UTC collection time, well beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, and was therefore not relied upon; independent research covered the same ground.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours opened with Tail already elevated at 26% during the Sep 1 European session, peaking at 31% around that day's US cash open as the US-Iran escalation, the crude surge and the sovereign-yield selloff were priced in. Tail then decayed through the US afternoon and the Asian handover and has held a 20-23% band for the last twelve published hours, while Stress stayed persistently high in a 69-77% range. That profile describes a difficult, high-volatility environment in which retracements kept occurring rather than a sustained one-way trend. Three hourly slots have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 20-24% band for most of the next 24 hours and lifts it above the block threshold only for the three-hour catalyst cluster from 12:00 to 15:00 UTC, covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with the single highest reading of 28% in the 13:00 UTC hour containing the opening auction. One further hour reaches the threshold at 21:00 UTC around the Broadcom results, where a top-weight semiconductor constituent can move the complex in a thin post-close book. Stress stays high throughout on the crude, sovereign-yield and Fed-repricing backdrop, which is structural rather than intraday, and eases only gradually through the Asian session before ticking up again into the Sep 3 European morning ahead of ISM Services and Friday's payrolls. Confidence decays with forecast distance because no live price-path evidence exists for later windows at the assessment cutoff.

forecast.analysis: Pre-ADP positioning hour. Liquidity typically thins into the 12:15 UTC release, which widens spreads without yet establishing direction. Modelled Tail eases slightly because a pre-event drift is normally two-way; hypothetical post-release alignment is not counted as already observed.

forecast.analysis: ADP prints at 12:15 UTC into a market already pricing roughly a two-in-three chance of a September Fed increase. A firm labour print would stack onto the existing oil and yield impulse. That conditional stacking, not the release itself, is why modelled Tail crosses the block threshold for this hour.
drivers: ADP Employment Change (Aug) at 12:15 UTC is the week's first labour checkpoint
September 16 FOMC increase priced near 64%; a firm print would tighten that further

forecast.analysis: Highest modelled hour: the 13:30 UTC US cash open follows the ADP reaction by about 75 minutes. Opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure that denies mean reversion. Whether it appears is unobserved at the cutoff and is treated as a scenario, not a fact.

forecast.analysis: Broadcom reports after the US close with the call around this hour. AVGO is a top-weight NQ constituent and the AI-capex read-through can move the whole semiconductor complex in a thin post-close book. That specific mechanism lifts modelled Tail to the block threshold for one hour.
drivers: Broadcom (AVGO) Q3 FY2026 results and call; a top-weight NQ and semiconductor name
A thin post-close futures book amplifies single-name repricing into the index
AI-capex guidance is the sector-level read-through, not just the headline print
